question: Should exec denylist policy use one canonical persisted surface, or remain unioned across both `openclaw.json` and `exec-approvals.json`?
rationale: Both are new public operator contracts with distinct editing, ownership, and upgrade semantics; implementation correctness cannot choose the permanent product boundary.

options.title: Use one canonical surface
options.body: Remove the competing persisted surface while retaining locked cross-host deny-over-allow enforcement.

options.title: Approve dual ownership
options.body: Keep both surfaces and explicitly support their deny-anywhere precedence, editing paths, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Pause the capability
options.body: Do not land the new authorization contract until maintainers sponsor its long-term ownership model.

recommendation.title: Use one canonical surface
recommendation.body: Remove the competing persisted surface while retaining locked cross-host deny-over-allow enforcement.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current-main ownership across all central exec authorization paths touched by this PR.
